messages:
Jordan (CS): FYI customer GlideAI (dedicated) reports lots of 429s from /v1/rerank since ~11:12 PDT. Happens on high-candidate calls (candidates=500-700). They say it started after traffic ramp.
Alex (Infra): @Jordan can you paste a sample request + response headers? curious if we're hitting a per-client QPS cap or a burst limiter.
Jordan (CS): Here’s a sanitized curl they sent: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -d '{"query":"...","candidates":[...600 items...]}'`
Jordan (CS): Response headers include: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, `x-redwood-rate-limit: 1000`, `x-redwood-rate-remaining: 0`, `retry-after: 2`
Pat (Eng): Interesting — header showing limit 1000 (per minute?) but remaining 0 right when they hit. Are they doing very large parallelism? client QPS spikes during the ramp?
Jordan (CS): Customer says they parallelize 40 workers and each sends batches of 600 candidates every ~3s for a short burst (30s) when a sync job runs.
Alex (Infra): That explains it. Our rerank path has a separate QPS guard for heavy-candidate requests to protect the KV cache and batching pools. Large candidate lists get a stricter concurrency window. Not a bug, more of a protective quota.
Susan (Support): They expected only token- or request-count billing and didn’t realize rerank has candidate-size throttles. Need clear messaging and a remediation plan before we reply.
Pat (Eng): Quick mitigations: 1) ask them to reduce parallel workers or stagger backoff, 2) send smaller candidate batches (<=200) and combiner on client side, 3) we can temporarily bump their per-tenant quota for dedicated if ops approves.
Alex (Infra): I’ll check metrics for that tenant id and confirm if quota bump is possible. @ops-bot can you open an incident for quota escalation (low priority) and attach the tenant id + sample request?
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-241234-qaescalate. Assigned to infra oncall.
Jordan (CS): Customer asks for repro steps so they can test fixes. Pat, can you propose minimal repro they can run locally?
Pat (Eng): Repro: run 10 parallel clients, each POSTing a 250-candidate rerank every 1s for 30s -> observe 429 tail. If you increase candidate count to 600 and keep concurrency you’ll see the throttle trigger quicker. Include `-H "X-Request-ID: repro-<n>"` to trace.
Alex (Infra): Also capture these metrics on our side: `rerank.requests_per_min`, `rerank.large_candidate_concurrency`, `rerank.429_rate` for the tenant. I’ll attach graphs in the incident.
Susan (Support): Reply draft to customer: short explanation + action items (stagger workers / reduce batch size / temporary quota bump possible). I'll wait for infra confirmation before sending.
Jordan (CS): Customer accepted staged plan: they will reduce batch size to 200 and implement exponential backoff. If that still hits we proceed with quota bump.
Pat (Eng): Long term: we should add clearer error body for 429 on rerank indicating "candidate_count" throttle and include suggested backoff/batch sizes. Filing a small request in product backlog.
Alex (Infra): ETA: I’ll have tenant metrics and a ratchet suggestion within 45m. Ops oncall will review quota bump.
Susan (Support): Thanks — I’ll hold the customer update until we have ops answer. :thumbsup:
Jordan (CS): Closing loop here once ops confirms. Thanks team. :eyes:
